evidence: The paper explicitly uses Gini-based importance: "The Gini index served as the performance metric for this assessment." It interprets importance magnitude and ranking to support key conclusions: "with BIW_i standing out as the most relevant factor, particularly for high specificity values" and "the prediction factor WW_i replaced birthweight-related factors as the most relevant, accounting for more than 50% of the importance." The importance rankings are corroborated through partial dependence plots ("Partial dependence plots were examined for factors accounting for more than 5% importance") and held-out validation showing AUC reduction when high-importance factors are excluded ("resulting in a decrease in AUC ranging from 0.056 to 0.060").
